subject: ANGL
title: English Language – Form 2
source: Form 2 syllabus by week (30 weeks, 4 h/week); dates worked out from the school calendar

chapters.title: Module 1: Satisfying basic daily needs (15 h)

lessons.title: Week 1: Using public transportation – simple present tense; prepositions of movement; sounds /ʃ/ and /ʒ/
Week 2: Consulting health professionals – modals and polite expressions; sounds /i/ and /iː/
Week 2: Preparing and ordering meals – connectives of order and sequence; sounds /ʌ/ and /ɑ/
Week 3: Ordering meals; being informed about the weather, news and sports – adverbs of frequency and manner; idioms
Week 4: Treating illnesses and taking medication – modals expressing obligation; writing an informal letter
Week 5: Using the telephone; shopping – imperatives; present continuous tense; writing a shopping list
Week 6: Revision, evaluation and remediation

chapters.title: Module 2: Involvement in community activities and concerns (20 h)

lessons.title: Week 7: Participating in community work – simple sentences, simple past, active and passive voice; stress on two-syllable words
Week 8: Celebrating public national holidays – present perfect; punctuation (exclamation mark, colon)
Week 9: Rights and duties of the child; young parliamentarians – question tags; active and passive voice
Week 10: Setting up a neighbourhood watch – past perfect tense; prefixes denoting opposites; sounds /θ/ and /ð/
Week 11: Volunteering and community service – compound sentences (cause and effect); abstract, concrete, countable and uncountable nouns
Week 12: Revision, evaluation and remediation

chapters.title: Module 3: Gaining access to and using public services (20 h)

lessons.title: Week 13: Accessing healthcare services using ICT – affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences; ICT register
Week 14: Accessing popular education services – modals of possibility, obligation, ability and permission; the formal letter
Week 15: Garbage collection and disposal; postal services – imperatives (revision); addressing an envelope, money order form
Week 16: Using library services; recreational services – reported speech
Week 17: Recreational centres, banks and financial institutions – connectors, conditionals (type two); sounds /e/ and /eɪ/
Week 18: Revision, evaluation and remediation

chapters.title: Module 4: Current global issues in the media (20 h)

lessons.title: Week 19: Finding out about scientific developments – comparatives and superlatives
Week 20: Exploring issues related to pollution – expressing opinions (believe, think); sounds /ɔ/ and /ɔː/
Week 21: Violence and corruption at school and in the community – coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
Week 22: Exploring the world of entertainment – comparative adverbs; writing a poster
Week 23: Healthcare issues: HIV/AIDS, cholera, malaria – punctuation (comma, exclamation mark, colon)
Week 24: Revision, evaluation and remediation

chapters.title: Module 5: Exploring cultural issues and practices (20 h)

lessons.title: Week 25: Film shows and concerts by national artists – future tense
Week 26: Attending festivals – simple past and past perfect (revision); descriptive adjectives
Week 27: Visiting museums and handicraft centres – collective nouns
Week 28: Exploring traditional dance – future tense, relative pronouns; sounds /s/ and /z/
Week 29: Gender roles – indefinite and possessive pronouns; sounds /tʃ/ and /dʒ/
Week 30: Revision, evaluation and remediation; general revision and end-of-year evaluation
